text:
**You need roughly 200-300 W of solar to recharge a 1,000 Wh station in one to two days of decent sun.** Going bigger mostly helps in winter or cloudy weather.

**The formula:** panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charging losses, since panels rarely deliver their rated watts ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Full recharge from empty in one day (1,000 Wh):**

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts needed |
|---|---|
| 3 | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 | ~230 W |

These come from [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) gives about 300 W in summer and about 735 W in a northern winter (2 sun hours).

**If you'd rather take more than a day:**
- **200 W panel:** about 630 Wh per day at 4.5 sun hours, so a little over 1.5 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- **400 W panel:** about 1,260 Wh per day, so under a day ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Rule of thumb:** capacity ÷ 5 gives the panel wattage for a full recharge in about a day and a half, so 200 W for 1,000 Wh.

**Check these before buying:**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps how many watts it accepts. Entry-level units often cap at 100-200 W, and mid-range 1,000-1,500 Wh units typically allow 400-800 W. Panel wattage above the cap adds nothing in strong sun.
- **Voltage window:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay within your station's input range. Exceeding it can damage the charge controller, and wiring panels in series adds their voltages.
- **Connectors:** Panels usually have MC4 connectors, so make sure you have the right adapter for your station.
- **Using power while charging:** Any load you run during the day reduces the net recharge.

If you want a single 400 W panel, one option is the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel). It lists at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 per the listing, and the store's checkout has the final word on price. It has a 45.3 V Voc, so confirm your station accepts that voltage and 400 W before ordering. It also weighs 18.5 kg. The retailer's link is an affiliate link.
